title: Driftwing dragon audit — standard capture set
intro: The wyverns as an expert reviewer needs to see them: portraits, flight poses, motion as labelled frame sequences (contact sheets), surface close-ups, light response, in-game views, distance/LOD, ghost and cosmetics, plus measurements. Showcase shots use ?view=wyvern with the real sky (sky=native), quality=high, clear weather and golden hour (tod 0.7) unless noted. Every staging uses fresh=1 (default look, animation restarted from rest) and blink=999 (any idle cue holds the random blinks, membrane sweeps and tongue flicks off, so stills repeat exactly; the head strips cue them on purpose). Strip frames are at a fixed simulated time step; frame labels give the strip time and the state that matters (flap phase, gait phase, mode/gait/height/airspeed/pitch/bank). Azimuths are relative to the wyvern's heading: 0 = in front, 90 = its left side, 180 = behind.

sections.title: c. Motion strips — contact sheets at a fixed simulated time step
sections.note: The wingbeat strips run continuous time from rest for three beats, then capture one full beat in 12 frames (phase 0 at frame 0); the onion skin composites every frame's moving parts over the median background to show the wingtip and body arcs. Walk/run capture one gait cycle (period from the gait's own cycle length and speed). Takeoff, landing, turn and dive drive the REAL player and flight model (real=) with scripted input; their labels give mode/gait, height above ground, airspeed, pitch and bank. Light vs heavy: harrier and ironback.
